findings.claim: The move of extract_exif above the row writes does not take it out of the write lock on the trashed-ghost path, because that path flushes a delete and runs cleanup_orphan_tags before the read, and the new lock test covers only a fresh upload.
findings.impact: When a trashed row's file has gone from disk and a large PNG without an eXIf chunk is uploaded to that path, other writers wait while the PNG decodes, and with the default 5 second busy timeout could fail with 'database is locked'. This is rare: a normal trash keeps the file on disk, so init_upload answers 409 and the path is not reached.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/upload.py:288-296 runs db.delete(existing), db.flush() and cleanup_orphan_tags; extract_exif runs afterwards at :308; the commit is at :371. backend/app/services/fileops.py:671-687 shows the soft delete keeps the file on disk, and upload.py:136-137 rejects a live path, so the ghost needs the file removed outside the app while it is in the trash. backend/tests/test_exif.py test_reading_an_upload_holds_no_write_lock uploads only a new a.png. read_image_dimensions at :306 has the same placement and predates this change.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Predicted: trash a.png through the API, unlink it from disk, then run the test's stubbed extract_exif during an upload to a.png. writable should be [False]. Commands cannot be run in this review.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. The result stays correct, and the cost appears only on a rare path with a large PNG and a concurrent writer.

findings.proposed_fix: Compute dimensions and exif before the `if existing is not None and existing.deleted_at is not None` block, and add the ghost case to the lock test.

findings.claim: The EXIF call in register_single_file is still not asserted by any test, although the new scan test closes the other two scanner call sites.
findings.impact: A photo brought in through note image import reaches the library through this function. If its EXIF call broke, that photo would silently have no Photo Info until a later scan backfilled it, and no test would fail.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/scanner.py:387-389 calls extract_exif and adds the row. backend/app/services/markdown_image_import.py:416 is its production caller. A grep of backend/tests for '/exif', 'file_exif' and 'extract_exif' matches only test_exif.py and two database migration or rebuild test files. A grep for register_single_file across backend/tests, limited to its first 30 matches, showed no hit in test_exif.py, and the test_exif.py diff imports only _scan_and_register. The callers listed in test_image_dimensions.py, test_scanner.py and others are outside the EXIF match set.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Predicted mutation, not run: delete scanner.py:387-389. No test should fail, because no test asserts a file_exif result after register_single_file. Deleting :549-552 or :754-756 should now fail test_a_scan_reads_a_photo_it_finds_and_one_with_no_exif_row.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. This is the remainder of the r1 coverage findings CR-1 and DEEP-1; the code reads correct and a later scan would backfill the row.

findings.proposed_fix: Add to TestEveryWayIn a test that calls register_single_file on a HEIC with EXIF and asserts the /exif response.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so bucket A is unavailable and there is no touch-point list to compare against.

No approved spec was consulted for this behavior. The earlier review record reports no spec entry for heic or exif, and the new tests mark their behavior with UNSPEC comments. I did not search docs/specs again.
r1 CR-2 is addressed: the TIFF case is now in test_exif_is_read_from_every_container, which also catches moving get_ifd out of the `with` block, by reading of how TIFF loads tags lazily.
r1 CR-1 and DEEP-1 are addressed for scanner.py:549-552 and :754-756, and not for :387-389 (CR-6).
r1 CR-3 and DEEP-2 are addressed for a new upload and a reused row, and not for the trashed-ghost path (CR-5).

r1 CR-4 and DEEP-4 are unchanged by the fix: the scanner still fills only absent rows, and a copy still inherits the source row. Neither is restated as a new finding. No code in fba3915ca touches them.
decisions.md records its app run at be9a0fcb0, before the extract_exif move in fba3915ca, so that run does not exercise the commit's upload ordering, and it times no PNG.
potential_unspecified_behavior: An upload extracts EXIF immediately, and an upload over a reused row deletes the old row even when the new file has no EXIF (upload.py:355-360).
A copy duplicates the source's EXIF row, GPS included and across drives, without reading the copied file (fileops.py:298-313).
TIFF files with EXIF tags now get file_exif rows, now pinned by a test but still with no approved spec (exif.py:69-72).
Image formats with no _getexif, such as BMP and GIF, now return None without the warning they used to log, a log-only change.

A SVG or other .image-classified file Pillow cannot open now logs an 'EXIF extraction failed' warning at upload as well as at scan, a log-only change, if such a file reaches upload.py:308; the classification was not traced.
regression_risks: A large PNG without an eXIf chunk is now decoded twice during POST /complete, once in read_image_dimensions and once in extract_exif, both outside the lock on the normal path. The latency is unmeasured, since decisions.md item (6) timed only JPEG and HEIC.

A scan's pending db.merge(FileExif) at scanner.py:552 could conflict with an upload committing a row for the same id before the scan's flush. This needs an upload over a row with no EXIF landing during a scan, so it is narrow; it was recorded in r1 and is unchanged by the fix. Not reproduced.

A photo whose ISOSpeedRatings holds several values makes int(iso_raw) at exif.py:107 raise, and the outer except drops all its EXIF. This is pre-existing, but more formats now reach the line. No real phone HEIC has been exercised.

A photo moved outside the app and matched by hash in scanner Pass 2 skips the EXIF backfill for that scan (scanner.py:657-706), so a pre-fix HEIC moved that way gets its row only on the following scan.
test_coverage: test_reading_an_upload_holds_no_write_lock tries BEGIN IMMEDIATE on a second connection from inside the stubbed extract_exif. Moving the call back after the flush at upload.py:352 should make writable [False], so that mutant is predicted killed. The test runs without the WAL mode production sets, but a held write lock blocks BEGIN IMMEDIATE in either mode, so the check still applies.

test_a_scan_reads_a_photo_it_finds_and_one_with_no_exif_row covers both Pass 2 (scanner.py:754) and the Pass 1 backfill (:549) with a HEIC, using /exif. Deleting either block should fail it at a different assertion.
test_exif_is_read_from_every_container now covers JPEG, HEIF, WEBP and TIFF with values in the root, Exif and GPS IFDs.
test_a_copied_photo_has_the_same_exif compares whole /exif responses, so dropping a response field from the copy in fileops.py:301-312 should fail it.

Deleting only the db.flush() at upload.py:358 would probably survive, because SQLAlchemy can turn a delete and add of one primary key in a single flush into an update; the visible behavior would stay the same.

Not covered: EXIF after register_single_file (CR-6), the lock on the trashed-ghost path (CR-5), upload over a trashed row asserting EXIF, a PNG containing EXIF, batch_copy, and a copy to another folder or drive. The last two share copy_file's code with the tested same-folder copy.

Real phone HEIC files were not checked.
Decode time and lock wait for a large PNG were not measured.

docs/process/review.md, testing-and-comments.md, backend-conventions.md and docs/specs were not read; only .claude/rules/process.md was.
The classification of SVG files at upload and addon code paths were not traced.
trajectory: Two commits follow r1. fba3915ca moves one existing line, the extract_exif call, from after the flush to beside read_image_dimensions in upload.py, and adds tests: a TIFF parameter, a lock test and a scan test. 7a68cc9ac adds only review documents. Neither adds a branch, a state or a prediction in production code, so this round does not repeat what the round before it added and the design is not being patched. Neither removes one either: the delete-and-replace branch and the copy branch from before r1 remain as they were. The move leaves one path behind (CR-5), which comes from where the line was placed and not from a new condition.
